title: NORD-10 I/O device card: connector to the backplane

sources.document: Backwiring til NORD-10 (A/S Norsk Data-Elektronikk): connector specification list, connector lists per card position, signal code list
sources.note: Typed wiring list of the NORD-10 CPU crate. The connector lists of A22 and A25 were checked against the page images; the OCR of the other slot pages agrees with them pin for pin.

sources.document: NORD-10 drawings, sheet 2A50 SYNCHRONOUS MODEM BUFFER 1050 (1973), as read pin by pin in this repository (sheets/nord-10/2A50-sync-modem-buffer-1050.rsc, docs/2A50-reading.md)
sources.note: The names the card drawing uses (LEV10, IOXE, MC ...) differ from the backplane names (BINT10, BIOXE, BMCL ...); the pin numbers match.

sources.document: ND-06.008.01 NORD-10/S Reference Manual, Revision A
sources.note: Sections 3.3 (IOX), IDENT instruction, 4.1 (Input/Output hardware) and 4.1.3 (vectored interrupt identification). It refers to the NORD-10 Input/Output manual ND-06.004 for signal levels, definitions and timing; that manual was NOT found on this machine.

name.note: No NORD-10 document found names the card connector(s) (no A/B/C letters). The A/B/C plug letters are documented for NORD-100 modules only.

connectorsPerCard.note: The backwiring list has one connector per card position (read). The 2A50 board (322049) has one gold-finger edge along its backplane side with 50 fingers on each side, 100 in all, which fits one 0-99 connector (read on the photos; that it is one connector is inferred). See fingers.

power.note: Power pins are not in the backwiring list. 62/63 and 66/67 on 2A50 are outputs of the card's own +-12V converter, not supply in. +5V pin open.

note: NORD-10/S manual section 4.1.1: 'Cable connectors are plugged directly into the backplane' and 'Device plugs are also to a common standard' (read). Every circled pin on 2A50, bus and modem alike, is a pin of this one 0-99 connector, written P.n (owner's decision 2026-11-23); 6-55 is the bus side, 56-99 the cable side (inferred). The former separate file nord10-modem-front.json is merged in here as the 81-95 rows.

pinMap.note: Every pin 0-99 once. side and finger: where the gold finger is (see fingers). signal, direction, active and description come from catalog/signals/nd-bus-nord10.json for bus pins, from the 2A50 rows above for the modem pins, and say empty where the backwiring list has nothing. on2A50 = the signal name sheet 2A50 gives the pin (absent = 2A50 does not use it).

fingers.value: 50 gold fingers on each side, 2.54 mm (0.1 inch) apart, each opposite one on the other side. Even pins on the component side, odd pins on the solder side: seen from the component side with the fingers at the top, finger k from the left (k = 0..49) is pin 2k, and the finger behind it on the solder side is pin 2k+1. So pin 0 and pin 1 are at the left end (component view), 98 and 99 at the right end.
fingers.source: photos of board 322049 (2A50), ND PCB catalogue; checked against the 2A50 drawing
proof: Count: 50 fingers on each side, measured on both new photos of 322049 (READ from the photos). Pitch 2.546 mm on the solder photo, 2.58 mm on the component photo (photo scale); 0.1 inch INFERRED.

Ground: on the component side the vias of fingers 40, 41, 42, 43 (counted from the left, from 0) are joined, and a wide trace joins 43 to 47. The drawing ties exactly five circled pins to ground: 80, 82, 84, 86, 94 = 2 x 40, 41, 42, 43, 47 (READ on the photo, matches the drawing).
BA0, pin 32: component finger 16 -> via -> solder-side trace -> via -> component trace -> 11C (7404, marked 7404 on the chip) pin 3. The drawing has BA0 = P.32 = 11C.3 (READ on the photos).
BA1, pin 33: the solder-side finger behind component finger 16 -> solder trace -> via -> component trace -> 11C pin 1. The drawing has BA1 = P.33 = 11C.1 (READ on the photos).

Use pattern: of the 50 solder-side fingers, 46 agree with "odd pin 2k+1 is used on 2A50 or not"; the next best rule (pins 2k on that side) agrees on 39, any 0-49 / 50-99 split on 27 or fewer. The four that disagree are pins 1 and 99 (wide copper at both ends, a supply, not on the drawing), 9 (INGRANT, joined straight to pin 8) and 11 (IOXE, trace not followed to its end).
fingers.open: Which pins carry +5V and ground from the backplane (candidates 0, 1, 98, 99 and 60, 64 by their wide copper); whether every NORD-10 card follows the same rule (checked on 2A50 only); the finger length and width (about 8 mm and 1.5 mm, measured on one photo).
